summary: Boise NF ground lookout in Valley County: 16x16 cabin dated 1934, last used 1942, destroyed 1950; only debris by 1988.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1950 per all three lookout pages; only a pile of debris remained by 1988.

staffing.status: no documented staffing history; last used in the 1942 fire season

access.note: On Boise National Forest land. No source says the site is closed or restricted, and none describes the site today.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site hike-in. The climbing guide says the trail to the summit has not been maintained for many years; its access notes carry an 'Updated January 2020' line.

events.note: Forest Lookouts: the site began in the 1930s with an alidade and a tent camp. Decade only, no exact year.
16 x 16 ft cabin. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts call it a frame cabin; Forest Lookouts calls it a tent cabin in one entry and dates a non-standard cabin to the mid-1930s in another.
Forest Lookouts: the last fire season the lookout was used. No staffing names are given in any source.
All three lookout pages date destruction to 1950.
Forest Lookouts: only a pile of debris remains. The climbing guide's author visited the Stolle Peak summit that year and found little of the structure left.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts call the 1934 cabin a 16 x 16 ft frame cabin; Forest Lookouts calls it a tent cabin in one entry and a non-standard cabin in another. The story reports the disagreement and does not choose.

The 1953 USGS station description places the benchmark at an abandoned lookout about two miles southwest of Cougar Rock. The climbing guide ties a 1934-1950 lookout to the summit it calls Stolle Peak, which the current USGS map labels Cougar Rock Benchmark. No source confirms that the lookout stood on the peak named Cougar Rock.

notes_for_editor: Location is unsettled. The record's FFLA coordinates (44.58538, -115.7296) and the Idaho Fire Lookouts coordinates (44.59795, -115.7204) are about 1.6 km apart, and no source fixes the lookout summit. The 1953 benchmark note places the station 2 miles SW of Cougar Rock, while the climbing guide ties the lookout to Stolle Peak, which it says the USGS map calls Cougar Rock Benchmark. Verify the pin before using it. Access level 'public' is an inference from national forest land and the absence of any closure notice, not a source statement. The FFLA list gives no location note.
